nativeMemoryObservation.scope: Native parser allocation observation only; not browser RSS/PSS, JavaScript memory, retained pipeline memory or whole-import peak memory.

purpose: One-pass complete parser output parity; no timing or browser import claim
limitations: One pass per arm validates complete parser output equality. No import timing was measured and no speed improvement is claimed.

The experiment does not validate browser storage bytes, persisted-content decoding, media blob writes, restart behavior, or actual whole-import completion. Separate exact-SHA browser qualification is required.
Equal maximum WASM memory lengths do not establish browser or pipeline memory neutrality. The candidate adds a fixed 1,040-byte call-local stack cache.

The initial all-corpus process completed JMdict and Jitendex, then was killed with exit 137 while opening VNDB before any VNDB row result. Those completed results were retained; the incomplete VNDB attempt is not a passing observation.
VNDB was rerun separately using file-backed ZIP reads, an entry generator, ten-bank groups, and a 640 MiB JavaScript heap cap.

The first file-backed VNDB attempt stopped after the baseline parser legitimately omitted prepared lookup indexes on a fallback group. The harness assertion was corrected to permit and hash optional index presence; the subsequent complete pass produced the reported VNDB result.

The two oracle programs have distinct recorded SHA-256 values because VNDB used the corrected file-backed reader and optional-index handling. Digest equality is asserted within each corpus, not between different corpora or oracle programs.
